reason: The first HydroLAKES PMTiles stores the exact Hylak_id in MVT Feature.id; Tippecanoe --use-attribute-for-id removes the redundant property. The original property-presence expectation therefore fails. Preserve that failed attempt and evaluate the native feature-ID representation explicitly.

asset_contract.meaning: MVT Feature.id is the authoritative encoded value of the named source ID column. No inferred spatial join or reassigned identifier is permitted.

acceptance: Every encoded MVT ID must be a safe exact integer and equal the source Hylak_id. Complete source-ID coverage/accounting remains required.
For this encoding only, normalize the named source ID property from the already checked MVT Feature.id before exact attribute comparison and UI display. An existing contradictory property fails.
Every other selected source attribute and bbox scalar must still compare exactly, with the same documented null-omission behavior.
The 30m geometry tolerance, fixed geographic samples, immutable source pins and partial-read browser requirements remain unchanged.
The viewer must expose Hylak_id from Feature.id and successfully fetch all source attributes with that exact ID and original bbox.
Other new datasets retain their ID both in Feature.id and properties; no global skipping of ID checks.
reproducibility: The adopted recipe explicitly records --use-attribute-for-id Hylak_id. Retain original structural/header-check failure and do not call it a passing property-presence check. New candidate metadata binds original archive bytes and all subsequent validation reports.
